name: Micron Technology, Inc.

profile.description: Micron designs and manufactures DRAM, NAND and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for data center, mobile, PC and automotive markets, headquartered in Boise, Idaho. FY2026 revenue reached $133.2B (up 256%) with Q4 revenue of $54.2B (+379% YoY) and data-center revenue up 11-fold [1].

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): Micron exited consumer RAM (Crucial) to redirect capacity to HBM and AI server memory, producing FY2026 revenue of $133.2B versus $37.4B in FY2025 [1][2]. AI Deployment (2/2): HBM and data-center DRAM ship to AI customers, with data-center revenue up 11x [2]. Market Share (2/2): one of three global DRAM/HBM leaders with record share in AI memory. Product Pipeline (2/2): fiscal Q1 revenue guided to ~$61.5B with expanded capacity and supply tightness expected through FY2027-28 [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): R&D as a percent of revenue has fallen sharply relative to the revenue surge, below the sector's top quartile.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): 'transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all' is specific and tied to decades of memory leadership. Community Impact (1/2): Micron Foundation programs and community investment, without dollar-specific figures located. Employee Retention (1/2): 81% say it is a great place to work, but reviews cite rigid culture and abrupt role eliminations after long tenure [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): no net insider buying evidence found [3].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock (yield well under 2%; 5yr CAGR and PEG unavailable and excluded). D/E of 3.7% (1.0), ROE of 88.3% (1.0, 2x weight), revenue growth of 379% (1.0), forward P/E of 5.2 (1.0) and 63.8% profit margin (1.0) all meet or exceed targets, for 6.0/6 and a score of 10 [1]. Dollar volume of ~$36B gives maximum liquidity.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (9/9): Micron is AI infrastructure; HBM and DRAM demand rises with AI adoption and analysts see memory shortages, not substitution, with supply tight through FY2028 [1][2]. The risk is cyclical capex overbuild, not AI disruption. AI Opportunity (1/1): data-center revenue up 11x with FY2026 revenue of $133.2B and RPO of ~$150B tied to AI memory [1][2].

infinite_game.summary: Micron's decades of memory leadership and willingness to exit consumer products (Crucial) to serve AI customers show real existential flexibility and courage. Its cyclical, capacity-driven business and mixed employee feedback keep it short of a pure infinite-game example.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): enriching life through information is a genuine, distinctive cause lived across memory cycles, though less tested as a cause than as an engineering franchise [2].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): CEO Sanjay Mehrotra has held the role since 2017 with 90%+ Glassdoor approval, but reviews report a rigid culture and layoffs [3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): competitive language centres on technology and share leadership against SK hynix and Samsung with no learn-from-rivals framing.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): reinvention from commodity PC DRAM to AI-centric HBM and the Crucial exit abandoned a profitable consumer brand to serve the data center [2].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (2/2): exiting the consumer Crucial business and committing massive capex to HBM capacity, a pattern repeated through past downturns, trades near-term revenue for long-term capability [2].

investment_thesis: Micron at $1,074.89 trades at only 5.2x forward earnings after FY2026 revenue of $133.2B (+256%), Q4 revenue of $54.2B (+379%), adjusted FY EPS of $75.52 (+811%), a 63.8% profit margin and 88% ROE with D/E of 3.7% [1]. Q1 FY2027 guidance of ~$61.5B revenue and EPS of $38.15, a $32B customer-commitment backlog, and RPO of ~$150B under long-term supply agreements give unusual visibility [1][2].
thesis_continued: Memory is historically boom-bust: a slowdown in AI capex or capacity overbuild could compress prices from peak margins, and a 5x forward P/E signals the market already prices cyclical normalisation [2]. Customer concentration, geopolitical exposure to Asian supply chains and worker-rights risks, plus a MISALIGNED faith score (-49, LGBT Activism), are additional concerns [3].
key_catalysts: HBM and AI data-center demand driving fiscal Q1 revenue guidance of ~$61.5B [1]
Long-term supply agreements with $32B customer commitments and ~$150B RPO [1][2]
Supply tightness through FY2027-28 with capacity expansion [1]
key_risks: Memory cyclicality: an AI capex slowdown or capacity overbuild could reverse record margins [2]
Customer concentration and rapidly evolving AI architectures changing memory requirements [2]
Geopolitical and supply-chain labor risks in Asia plus rigid-culture talent risk [3]

backlog.note: Total reflects remaining performance obligations (~$150B, up from ~$100B last quarter); funded figure is $32B of customer commitments under long-term supply agreements. Quarterly revenue is $54.2B. Book-to-bill is not reported.
